extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical celestial mechanics / Newtonian physics
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing how mutual attractions (especially inverse-square accelerative forces) among bodies affect area-time proportionality, orbital shape (approximate ellipticity), precession of apsides and nodes, and other perturbation phenomena in multi-body systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXVI (Theorema XXVI) — inverse-square accelerative attractions imply near-elliptic areas proportional to times
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpora ... vires decrescent in duplicata ratione distantiarum, & attractiones acceleratrices binorum quorumcunque inter se reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum; minora autem circa maximum revolvantur : dico quod interius circa intimum & maximum, radiis ad ipsum ductis, describet areas temporibus magis proportionales, & figeram ad formam ellipseos umbilicum in centro eodem habentis magis accedentem ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mutual accelerative attractions fall off as the square of distances (inverse-square law) and smaller bodies revolve about a dominant body, then the areas described about the inner and dominant centres with radii to them are more nearly proportional to times and the orbit approaches an ellipse with the common centre (umbilicus) — particularly the closer the system is to the pure inverse-square behaviour and the stronger/less perturbed the central action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. I — proximity of dominant body increases perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: In casu secundo, quo propius accedit corpus omnium maximum ad systema duorum vel plurium, eo magis turbabuntur motus partium systematis inter se; propterea quod linearum a corpore maximo ad has ductarum jam maior est inclinatio ad invicem, majorque proportionis inaequalitas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the large (dominant) body comes closer to the system of smaller bodies, mutual motions are more disturbed because the inclinations and inequalities of the lines from the maximum to the others increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 2 — non-inverse-square accelerations produce larger perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: Maxime autem turbabuntur, ponendo quod attractiones acceleratrices partium systematis versus corpus omnium maximum non sint ad invicem reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum a corpore illo maximo ; praesertim si proportionis hujus inaequalitas major sit quam inaequalitas proportionis distantiarum a corpore maximo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perturbations are greatest when the accelerative attractions toward the dominant body deviate from the inverse-square law; the larger the deviation of that proportionality (relative to geometric inequalities), the greater the perturbation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 3 — for near-circular/elliptical unperturbed motion, external accelerations must be minimal or symmetric
rubrics_metrics.description: Unde si systematis partes in ellipsibus, vel circulis sine perturbatione insigni moveantur; manifestum est, quod eaedem a viribus acceleratricibus, ad has corpora tendentibus, aut non urgentur nisi levissime, aut urgentur aequaliiter & secundum lineas paraHelas quamproxime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parts move in ellipses or circles with negligible perturbation, the accelerative forces acting toward those bodies must either be very small or act evenly and along as-parallel-as-possible directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: area/time proportionality most nearly preserved when third-body forces minimal
rubrics_metrics.description: Manifestum est, quod areae temporibus tum maxime fiunt proportionales, ubi vis tertia, manentibus viribus caeteris, fit minima; & quod orbis PAB tum maxime accedit ad praefatam formam ellipticam, ubi vis tam secunda quam tertia, sed praecipue vis tertia fit minima, vi prima manente.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The areas are most nearly proportional to times and the orbit most nearly elliptic when the perturbative (third-body) forces are as small as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case 2 — out-of-plane accelerations produce latitude perturbations proportional to MN
rubrics_metrics.description: Revolvantur jam corpora minora P, S circa maximum T in planis diversis; & vis L M agendo secundum lineam P T in plano orbitae P A B sitam ... vis altera N M agendo secundum lineam quae ipsi KS T parallela est ... inducet perturbationem motus in latitudinem, trahendo corpus P de plano suae orbitae. Et haec perturbatio ... erit ut vis illa generans M N, ideoque minima evadet ubi MN est minima.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When small bodies revolve in different planes, components of perturbing force acting out of the orbital plane induce latitude (inclination) perturbations; the magnitude scales with the effective MN component and is minimal when MN is minimal (i.e., when those attractions are more equal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 1 (later) — multiple small bodies reduce perturbation of inner body's motion when they attract the dominant equally
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex his facile coniitur, quod, si corpora plura minora P, S, R, &c. revolvantur circa maximum T, motus corporis intimi P minime perturbabitur attractionibus exteriorum, ubi corpus maximum T pariter a caeteris, pro ratione virium acceleratricum, attrahitur & agitatur, atque caetera a se mutuo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several small bodies revolve around a dominant, the inner body's motion is least perturbed when the dominant is drawn equally by the others (symmetry of attractions reduces perturbation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 2 (three-body) — third-body causes faster motion near conjunction/opposition than quadratures
rubrics_metrics.description: In systemate vero trium corporum T, P, S, si attractiones acceleratrices binorum quorumcunque in tertium sint ad invicem reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum; corpus P, radio PT, aream circa corpus T velocius describet prope conjunctionem A & oppositionem B, quam prope quadraturas C, D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a three-body system with inverse-square accelerations, a body describes area about the primary faster near conjunction/opposition because the net perturbing force accelerates motion in some intervals and retards in others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 3 — instantaneous speed variations: faster in conjunction/opposition than in quadratures
rubrics_metrics.description: Et eodem argumento patet quod corpus P, caeteris paribus, velocius movetur in conjunctione & oppositione quam in quadraturis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All else equal, third-body effects make the smaller body move faster at conjunctions/oppositions than at quadratures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 4 — curvature greater in quadratures than conjunctions/oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Orbita corporis P, caeteris paribus, curvior est in quadraturis quam in conjunctione & oppositione. Nam corpora velociora minus deflectunt a recto tramite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because bodies are faster near conjunction/opposition, they are deflected less from straight-line motion there; hence orbits appear more curved at quadratures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 5 — radial distance larger in quadratures than syzygies
rubrics_metrics.description: Unde corpus P, caeteris paribus, longius recedet a corpore T in quadraturis, quam in conjunctione & oppositione.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The body moves farther from the central body in quadratures than in conjunction/opposition under the same conditions (excluding excentricity effects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 6 — centripetal force variation and its effect on period (subduplicate relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoniam vis centripeta corporis centralis ... augetur in quadraturis per additionem vis LM, ac diminuitur in syzygiis per ablationem vis KL ... est autem vis illa centripeta ... in ratione composita ex ratione simplici radii TP directe & ratione duplicata temporis periodici inverse: patet hanc rationem compositam diminuI per actionem vis KL; ideoque tempus periodicum ... augeri, idque in subduplicata ratione ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition or subtraction of perturbing centripetal components (LM, KL) modifies the central effective centripetal force, and thereby changes the orbital period: decreasing centripetal force increases the period in a subduplicate ratio relative to the change in centripetal force and radius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 7 — apsidal (line of apsides) precession due to imbalance of perturbing forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex prsemissis consequitur etiam, quod ellipseos a corpore P descriptae axis, seu apsidum linea, quoad motum angularem, progreditur & regreditur per vices, sed magis tamen progreditur, & per excessum progressionis fertur in consequentia ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The line of apsides alternately advances and regresses due to the varying perturbing forces (LM, KL); overall tendency depends on relative magnitudes so that net progression often occurs when perturbations in syzygies exceed those in quadratures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 8 — apsidal movement tied to deviation of centripetal force from exact inverse-square
rubrics_metrics.description: Cum autem pendeat apsidum progressus vel regressus a decremento vis centripetae facto in majori vel minori quam duplicata ratione distantiae TP ... manifestum est quod apsides in syzygiis suis, per vim ablationem KL vel N M — L M, progredientur velocius, inque quadraturis suis tardius recedent per vim additionam LM ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apsidal motion (precession) depends on whether the centripetal force's change across the orbit differs from the exact inverse-square dependence; larger deviations near syzygies/ quadratures drive faster apsidal evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 9 — monotonic eccentricity change from persistent asymmetry in centripetal force variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Si corpus aliquod, vi reciproce proportional i quadrato distantiae suae a centro, revolveretur ... & mox, in descensu ab apside summa ad apsidem imam, vis illa per accessum perpetuum vis novse augeretur in ratione plusquam duplicata distantiae diminutae: manifestum est quod corpus ... magis vergeret in hoc centrum ... ideoque orbem describeret orbe elliptico interiorem ... Orbis igitur, accessu hujus vis novse, fiet magis excentricus. ... & contra diminuetur eadem, si ratio illa decrescat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, over successive revolutions, the centripetal force increases/decreases by amounts that grow/shrink faster than the inverse-square of distance change, eccentricity will monotonically increase/decrease; persistent asymmetric changes per revolution accumulate to alter eccentricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 10 — latitude perturbation (inclination) pattern by node location
rubrics_metrics.description: Ut rationem ineamus errorum in latitudinem, fingamus planum orbis E S T immobile manere; & ... vis ML agendo semper secundum planum orbis P A B, nunquam perturbat motus in latitudinem; quodque vis NM, ubi nodi sunt in syzygiis, agendo etiam secundum idem orbis planum, non perturbat hos motus; ubi vero sunt in quadraturis, eos maxime perturbat ... Unde fit ut corpore in syzygis existente inclinatio evadat omnium minima ... Inclinatio igitur ubi nodi sunt in syzygiis est omnium maxima. In transitu eorum a syzygiis ad quadraturas ... diminuitur; fitque omnium minima, ubi nodi sunt in quadraturis, & corpus in syzygiis ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perturbations of orbital inclination depend on node placement: when nodes are at syzygies certain perturbing components act in-plane and do not change latitude; when nodes are at quadratures out-of-plane forces produce maximal latitude changes. The inclination cycles accordingly with node motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 11 — nodes behavior: retreating at quadratures, stationary at syzygies
rubrics_metrics.description: Nodi igitur in quadraturis constituti perpetuo recedunt; in syzygiis, ubi motus in latitudinem nil perturbatur, quiescunt; in locis intermediis ... recedunt tardius: ideoque, semper vel retrogradi, vel stationarii singulis revolutionibus feruntur in antecedentia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes (points where orbit crosses reference plane) retreat (regress) when located at quadratures, remain stationary at syzygies, and exhibit intermediate behavior elsewhere; overall node motion is retrograde or stationary per revolution depending on configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 12 — conjunction produces slightly larger errors than opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Omnes illi in his corollariis descripti errores sunt paulo majores in conjunctione corporum P, S, quam in eorum oppositione; idque ob majores vires generantes NM & ML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors/perturbations are somewhat larger at conjunctions than at oppositions because the generating perturbing forces are larger in those configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 13 — scaling invariance: when S is large enough to be a central body for T & P, previous corollaries hold
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumque rationes horum corollariorum non pendeant a magnitudine corporis S, obtinent praecedentia omnia, ubi corporis S tanta statuitur magnitudo, ut circa ipsum revolvatur corporum duorum T & P systema. Et ex aucto corpore S, auctaque ideo ipsius vi centripeta ... evadent errores illi omnes, paribus distantiis, majores in hoc casu quam in altero, ubi corpus S circum systema corporum P & T revolvitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The qualitative corollaries remain valid regardless of S's absolute magnitude; if S is large enough to be the central body around which T & P revolve, the perturbations scale accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 14 — approximate scalings: NM, ML ~ radius and periodic-time relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cum autem vires NM, ML, ubi corpus S longinquum est, sint quamproxime ut vis SK vel ratio PT ad ST conjunctim ... manifestum est quod effectus illi omnes, stante corporum T & P systemate, & mutatis tantum distantia ST & vi absoluta corporis S, sint quamproxime in ratione composita ex ratione directa vis absolutae corporis S & ratione triplicata inversa distantiae S T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the distant body S is far, the perturbing forces scale approximately as S's absolute force times inverse-cube of distance; periodic effects scale with square of periodic times etc. These provide approximate scaling laws for perturbation magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 15 — similarity of effects under proportional changes: linear and angular errors scale with orbit diameters and periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Si, manentibus orbium ESE & PAB forma proportionibus & inclinatio ad invicem, mutetur eorum magnitudo & si corporum S & T vel maneant vel mutentur vires in data quavis ratione, hae vires ... agunt semper eodem modo, & eadem proportione: necesse est ut similes & proportionalia sint effectus omnes, & proportionalia effectuum tempora; hoc est ut errores omnes lineares sint ut orbium diametri, angulares vero iidem, qui prius, & errorum linearium similium vel angularium sequalium tempora ut orbium tempora periodica.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under uniform scaling (keeping shapes and inclinations), linear errors scale with orbit diameters and angular errors behave likewise; times scale with orbital periods. This gives similarity relations for perturbation effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 16 — error/time scaling for inner/outer bodies: angular errors of P scale with square of P's period and inverse square of T's period
rubrics_metrics.description: Errores lineares corporis P ... sunt, in singulis revolutionibus corporis illius P, ut quadratum temporis revolutionis quam proxime. ... errores angulares e centro T spectati ... erunt, in singulis revolutionibus corporis illius P, ut quadratum temporis periodici corporis P directe & quadratum temporis periodici corporis T inverse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linear errors per revolution scale approximately with the square of the revolution time; angular errors seen from T scale as (period_P)^2 / (period_T)^2. Hence relative periodic times determine perturbation magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 17 — representation of moderate force LM by radius PT and relation to median force
rubrics_metrics.description: Cum autem linea LM nunc major sit nunc minor quam radius PT, exponatur vis mediocris LM per radium illum PT; & erit haec ad vim mediocrem SK vel SN (quam exponere licet per ST) ut longitudo P T ad longitudinem ST. Est autem vis mediocris ... qua corpus T retinetur in orbe suo circum S, ad vim qua corpus P retinetur in orbe suo circum T, in ratione composita ex ratione radii ST & radium PT, & ratione duplicata temporis periodicorum ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may represent the moderate perturbing force LM by reference to radii PT and ST and periodic times; median perturbing forces relate by geometric ratios of distances and squared-period ratios — practical for estimating LM and MN from known periods and distances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 18 — fluid annulus model: rings nearer to T move faster in syzygies and oppositely in quadratures; nodes behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Visis legibus, fingamus corpora plura fluida circum idem T ad sequales ab ipso distantias moveri; deinde conflari annulum fluidum ... & singulae annuli partes ... propius accedent ad corpus T, & celerius movebuntur in conjunctione & oppositione ... quam in quadraturis. Et nodi annuli hujus ... quiescent in syzygiis; extra syzygias vero movebuntur in antecedentia, & velocissime quidem in quadraturis, tardius alibi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling many fluid rings concentric about T shows that ring-parts approach T and speed up at conjunction/opposition vs quadratures; nodes of such annuli are stationary at syzygies and move fastest at quadratures — useful qualitative model for ring/ fluid response to perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corols. 19–21 — globe-with-annulus and water-tide model: perturbing forces cause oscillatory water heights and node regressions tied to equatorial mass excess
rubrics_metrics.description: Fingas jam globum corporis T ... extendi usque ad hunc annulum ... contineat aquam, motuque eodem periodic o circa axem suum uniformiter revolvi. ... Vis LM trahet aquam deorsum in quadraturis, facietque ipsam descendere usque ad syzygias; & vis KL trahet eandem sursum in syzygils ... maxima aque altitudo evenire potest in octantibus post syzygias ... Corol. 21: materia globi juxta aequatorem redundans efficit ut nodi regrediantur ... per augmentum augetur iste regressus ... diminitur per diminutionem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a globe with a fluid annulus as an analogy: perturbing forces push fluid up/down cyclically producing tide-like flux; the locations of maximum/minimum heights depend on node positions relative to syzygies/quadratures. Excess equatorial mass causes node regression; reducing such mass reverses effect — an explanatory model for tidal and nodal phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 22 — inference about globe constitution from node motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Et inde vicissim, ex motu nodorum innotescit constitutio globi. Nimirum si globus polos eosdem constanter servat, & motus fit in antecedentia, materia juxta aequatorem redundat; si in consequentia, deficit ... Globus igitur homogeneus & perfectus non retinet motus plures distinctos, sed omnes componit & ad unum reducit ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From node motion one can infer mass distribution: persistent prograde node motion indicates equatorial excess; retrograde indicates deficit. A homogeneous globe reduces multiple imposed motions to a single uniform rotation; added mass asymmetries cause node evolution and pole wander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXVII (Theorema XXVII) — areas about center of gravity are more proportional to times; orbit about center of gravity more nearly elliptic
rubrics_metrics.description: Positis iisdem attractionum legibus, dico quod corpus exterius S, circa interiorum P, T commune gravitatis centricm O, radiis ad centrum illud ductis, describit areas temporibus magis proportionales & orbem ad formam ellipseos umbilicum in centro eodem habentis magis accedentem, qtiam circa corpus intimum & maximum T, radiis ad ipsum ductis, describere potest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing motion with respect to the common center of gravity O yields areas more nearly proportional to times and orbits closer to ellipses with that centre, than when describing about one interior body T — rationale: total attraction directs more nearly to the centre of mass than to one constituent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propositio LXVIII (Theorema XXVIII) — generalization: same conclusion holds with more interior bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Positis iisdem attractionum legibus, dico quod corpus exterius S^ circa interiorum Y & T commune gravitatis centrum O, radiis ad centrum illic ductis, describit areas temporibus, magis proportionales, & orbem ad formam ellipseos umbilicum in centro eodem habentis magis accedentem, si corpcs intimum & maximum his attractionibus perinde atque cetera agitetur, quam si id vel non attractum quiescat, vel multo magis aut multo minus attractum aut multo magis aut multo minus agitetur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends Prop. LXVII to more interior bodies: an external body's area-time proportionality and closeness to an elliptic form is improved when interior bodies are mutually attracted/act consistently (i.e., system behaves collectively) rather than when some interior bodies are fixed or differently active.
